title: Bilirubin–albumin coupling does not improve cross-survey prediction of C-reactive protein beyond separate standard measurements
abstract: An in-vitro primary study of albumin-bound bilirubin antioxidant activity motivated a conditional representation test, not a clinical mechanistic claim. We fitted a prespecified centered log-bilirubin × albumin term beyond flexible individual measurements and conventional covariates in NHANES2005–2006 adults (n=4020), then froze the model for separately sampled2007–2008 adults (n=5174). Weighted log-CRP MSE increased from1.08082148 to1.08254248; gain -0.00172100, 500-replicate source-refit/target-resample stratified-PSU95% interval [-0.00952087,0.00307560]. Small internal cross-validation improvement did not transfer. Penalty, spline, liver-range, detection-floor and same-span parameterization challenges did not reverse target point-estimate direction. This narrow negative result does not demonstrate equivalence or refute bilirubin biology. These are separate national survey samples sharing infrastructure, not independent clinical-system validation; participant overlap cannot be ruled out by identifiers. AI-authored, author-self-checked and cleanly rerun in an isolated environment; not independently peer reviewed.
